LMWG Meeting #3: Mitigation Actions –October16, 2025
Figure 4: LMS Working Group Meeting  #3 at the Santa Rosa County Emergency Operations Center
This meeting was facilitated by Diane Quigley and Courtney McMillion from Stantec, and Allara  
Mills-Gutcher from The Planning Collaborative at the Santa Rosa County Emergency Operations  
Center (F i g u re  4). The purpose of the meeting was to facilitate a working session with the LMS  
Planning Process  | 27

## [PDF page 28]
Working Group to reﬁne hazard rankings and proposed mitigation objectives and actions for  
inclusion in the 2026 update. Following completion of routine LMS business and the annual  
compliance review, the consultant team delivered a presentation outlining p roject progress,  
schedule, and next steps. Working Group members participated in an interactive hazard ranking  
exercise using an online polling platform, after which the group reviewed and discussed  
proposed revisions and additions to the LMS objectives and actions. The discussion included  
identifying new implementing agencies, updating supporting implementation documents, and  
reﬁning language for several objectives. The consultant team also reviewed proposed updates  
to the STAPLEE project scoring criteria and outlined upcoming opportunities for continued  
public engagement and local government review prior to submittal of the draft plan to the  
S tate .  
Citizen Engagement Session #2–October18, 2025
Figure 5: LMS Community Outreach Event  #2 at the Navarre Sand Dollar Market
Th is ou treach event was facilitated by Allara Mills-Gutcher from The Planning Collaborative and  
Courtney McMillion from Stantec. It served as the secon d and  ﬁn al citizen engagement activity  
conducted to introdu ce th e p lan u pd ate to members of  the p u blic and  solicit feed b ack on which  
of the 15 pre -identiﬁed hazards residents had personally experienced or were concerned about  
in th e f u ture.
A b ooth  was set u p at the Sand Dollar Market in Navarre,  wh i ch  d rew  ap proxi m ate l y 30  
members of the public (F i g u re  5). To  en co u rage engagement,  th e booth included a spinning  
Planning Process  | 28

## [PDF page 29]
wh eel and hazard-related prizes such as umbrellas, rain ponchos, and ﬂashlights.  T h e  eve nt  
aimed to:
•  Introduce the public to the hazard mitigation planning process;  
•  Document residents’ concerns and previous impacts related to the hazards;  
•  Distribute and collect responses to the survey.
Two poster sized boards were  displayed to document input from participants . On  th e ﬁrst  
board, residents placed a red sticker dot to indicate hazards they had been personally aﬀected  
b  y,  and a yellow sticker dot for hazards they were most concerned about in the future. On the  
second board, participants shared personal experiences, including tree damage, school closures  
from a recent winter storm, street ﬂooding, erosion impacts on ﬁshin g, and hail damage to  
vehicles.
Although QR codes lin king to the pu b lic su r vey were  d isp layed on  both poster boards,  
respondents were more comfortable completing the printed  copies of the s  u  r  v  e  y.  The  
consultant team also visited other vendor booths at th e market to invite participation, an d th is  
eﬀort added 27  co mp l ete d  s ur veys to the poll.  
Involving the Public
44 CFR Requirement  
44 CFR Part 201.6(b)(1): The planning process shall include an opportunity for the public to  
comment on the plan during the drafting stage and prior to plan approval.
An important component of the mitigation planning process involved public participation. Input  
from the community provides the entire LMWG with a greater understanding of local concerns  
and increases the likelihood of successfully implementing mitigation actions by developing  
community “buy-in” from those directly aﬀected by the decisions of County oﬃcials. As  
members of the community become more involved in decisions that aﬀect their safety, they are  
more likely to gain greater awareness of the hazards present in the County and surrounding  
jurisdictions and take the steps necessary to reduce their impact. Public awareness is a key  
comp on ent of any community ’s overall mitigation strategy aimed at making  th e County s a fe r  
from the potential eﬀects of hazards.

## [PDF page 29]
Pu b lic involvement d u ring th e d evelop ment of the Santa Rosa County Local Mitigation Strategy  
was sought using three methods: (1) two public citizen engagement sessions were held during  
the planning process as described above (2) a public survey was conduct  ed  (d escribed b elow)  
Planning Process  | 29

## [PDF page 30]
which permitted open comment; and (3) digital copies of the draft plan deliverables were made  
available and advertised for public review and comment on the County ’s website and the Plan’s  
Social Pinpoint site.
Th e p ub lic was p rovid ed  two opp ortun ities to b e involved  in  th e d evelop ment of th e Plan at two  
distinct periods during the planning process:  (1) during the drafting stage of the plan –  t wo  
public engagements; and (2) upon completion of a ﬁnal draft plan  – draft plan review, but prior  
to oﬃcial plan approval and adoption. A link to an electronic version of the draft plan was  
posted and advertised via the Plan Social Pinpoint Site for residents.  (November 10, 2025  –  
November 21, 2025). Appendix E d ocu ments these advertisements. Th e plan  was sent to  
oﬃcials with  Santa Rosa County and the Florida Department of Emergency Management for  
review and comment. The ﬁnal plan was reviewed and approved by  Santa Rosa Cou nty on  
MONTH DD, 2025 (the adoption resolution can be found in  Appendix A).  
Public Participation Survey  
The planning team was successful in getting community members to provide input to the  
mitigation planning process using a Public Participation Sur vey. The public sur vey was created to  
capture concerns and feedback from communities, especially those who might n ot be ab le to  
attend public meetings or participate through other means in the mitigation planning process.  
The sur vey was distributed both in paper format at the public tabling events, as well as online  
on the Plan’s Social Pinpoint site d istribu ted through the use of a QR Code  . T h e  su r vey  was  live  
from July to October 2025. Details for the Sur vey results can be found in Appendix D.

Involving the Public
44 CFR Requirement  
44 CFR Part 201.6(b)(1): The planning process shall include an opportunity for the public to  
comment on the plan during the drafting stage and prior to plan approval.
An important component of the mitigation planning process involved public participation. Input  
from the community provides the entire LMWG with a greater understanding of local concerns  
and increases the likelihood of successfully implementing mitigation actions by developing  
community “buy-in” from those directly aﬀected by the decisions of County oﬃcials. As  
members of the community become more involved in decisions that aﬀect their safety, they are  
more likely to gain greater awareness of the hazards present in the County and surrounding  
jurisdictions and take the steps necessary to reduce their impact. Public awareness is a key  
comp on ent of any community ’s overall mitigation strategy aimed at making  th e County s a fe r  
from the potential eﬀects of hazards.
